nodes.name: Pulsed Laser Deposition (PLD)
nodes.procedure: A metallic tungsten target was ablated in reactive atmosphere of oxygen at pressures ranging from 0.01 to 0.05 mbar using a frequency-tripled Nd:YAG laser (355 nm, 5 ns, 10 Hz) with fluence 4-8 J/cm². Substrates (Corning glass or Si(100)) positioned at 4 cm, temperature RT-600°C. Target rotated and translated for uniform ablation.

unit_operations.name: Laser Ablation
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: frequency-tripled SURELITE II Nd:YAG laser (wavelength 355 nm, pulse length 5 ns, repetition rate 10 Hz) ... laser fluence was in the range of 4-8 J/cm²

nodes.source_text: A metallic tungsten target was ablated in reactive atmosphere of oxygen... The deposition parameters are summarised in Table 1.

nodes.name: RF-Assisted Pulsed Laser Deposition (RF-PLD)
nodes.procedure: PLD process with added RF plasma beam source (13.56 MHz) generating excited/ionized oxygen beam through 2 mm nozzle. RF power 0-150 W applied during deposition on substrates at varying conditions per Table 1.

unit_operations.name: RF Oxygen Plasma
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: radio-frequency (13.56 MHz, CESAR 1310, RF maximum power 1000 W) power supply

nodes.source_text: addition to the PLD set-up of an excited and/or ionized beam of oxygen atoms... radio-frequency (13.56 MHz...)

nodes.characterization_summary: AFM shows RF beam addition results in more compact surface without droplets, smaller roughness around 1 nm, and diminished grain size for sample w621 compared to w619.
nodes.evidence_snippet: On a 20 μm × 20 μm scale, the surface of thin films deposited by RF-PLD is more compact, without droplets and with a smaller roughness, around 1 nm (Fig. 2).

nodes.characterization_summary: AES shows atomic concentrations for w83: W 51.3%, O 48.7%; w91: W 53.49%, O 46.51%; w92: W 38.5%, O 61.5%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the atomic concentrations of samples w83 and w91 are W 51.3 %, O 48.7 % and W 53.49 %, O 46.51 %, respectively... for sample w92 was recorded a W:O ratio of 38.5 %; 61.5 %.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns show no peaks related to crystalline WOx, suggesting nanocrystallites with very small dimensions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Although the X-ray patterns did not show any peak related to the formation of crystalline WOx, we can speculate that nanocrystallites with very small dimensions are present in our layers.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectra evolve from metallic tungsten (w71) to amorphous tungsten oxide (w72) with RF power, showing O-W-O bending modes (100-500 cm⁻¹) and W-O stretching (800 cm⁻¹), W=O stretching (950 cm⁻¹); higher temperature and lower fluence promote crystallization.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Looking at the spectra an evolution is observed from metallic tungsten (w71) to amorphous tungsten oxide (w72), associated to the operation of RF power.

nodes.characterization_summary: X-ray reflectivity on w72 gives density of 6.48 g cm⁻³ from critical angle, close to WO₃ bulk density of 7.2 g cm⁻³.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Preliminary X-ray reflectivity measurements... permitted... to get a density value of 6.48 g cm⁻³, which is close to WO₃ bulk density value (7.2 g cm⁻³).

nodes.characterization_summary: AFM shows dense, droplets and cracks free film at 400°C substrate temperature (w90/w91); clusters >500 nm at 200°C (w83); porous film at 600°C (w92).
nodes.evidence_snippet: A dense, droplets and cracks free film was obtained at 400 °C substrate temperature (Fig. 3b). For 200 °C substrate temperature clusters with diameter larger than 500 nm appeared on the film surface, while at 600 °C the film became porous (Fig. 3).

nodes.characterization_summary: AFM shows improved film quality with decreasing laser fluence from 8 to 3 J cm^{-2}, becoming more compact without droplets, lower roughness and porosity (w94, w90/w91, w95).
nodes.evidence_snippet: decreasing the laser fluence from 8 to 3 J cm^{-2}, the quality of the film surfaces was improved, becoming more compact, without droplets and with lower roughness and porosity (Fig. 4).
